newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- Mark vols bid, yen vols drop as dlr soars.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- Mark vols bid, yen vols drop as dlr soars.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options were well bid, while dollar/yen volatilities tinued sliding as the spot dollar rallied in hectic U.S. trading, dealers said.
The dollar, which have been climbing to new highs almost daily, leaped above the 1.7686-mark February 1994 high to 1.7742 marks today, the highest level since August 1991.
"We're making new highs (in dollar/mark), and it's been accelerating," a trader at a European bank said.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark stood at 8.5/8.8 percent in late trade, nearly half a point higher.

But interest in gamma was limited due to the dollar's grinding move higher and the upcoming weekend, keeping the volatility curve positive. Shorter-dated options have higher gamma, which makes them more spot-sensitive but vulnerable to time decay.
"It wasn't so much the short dates," an interbank broker said. He reported strong buying interest in the eight-month and one-year maturities.
Dollar/yen volatilities continued shrinking rapidly as the dollar rallied away from recent lows to more comfortable levels near 114 yen.
"Obviously, the market is less concerned about an imminent drop in dollar/yen," said Soma Rao, first vice president and options sales manager at Smith Barney.
That sense of relief was evident in a drastic shrinking in risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, which had been enormously skewed for yen calls in the past few months.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal was assessed at 1.7/2.0 percentage points in favor of yen calls. Earlier in the week, it had traded at an unprecedentedly wide 3.0 points.
Traders said such a level was just unsustainable without justification from actual spot movement.
One-month dollar/yen volatility fell a point to 9.3/9.6 percent.

News reports overnight that a former senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said U.S. and Japanese authorities could intervene if the dollar dropped below 110 yen also supported dollar sentiment, traders said.
"The market seems to think maybe that is the line in the sand," Rao said.
The dollar/yen curve, which had been inverted for a while, flipped back to positive as the longer maturities remained relatively resilient.
The interbank broker noted that even the shorter dates were still sensitive to any sign of dollar weakness.
"It's still a jittery market," he said. "If spot creeps below 113.50, offers are all running away very quickly."

Sterling volatilities were well bid as the pound made new highs against both the dollar and the mark. Cable rose to a six-month high of $1.6986, within a whisker of the $1.70 barrier, while sterling mark pushed above 3.00 marks for the first time in six years.
One-month cable volatility was a touch higher at 8.6/8.9 percent, while one-month sterling/mark gained a quarter point to 10.6/11.0 percent.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
